output.question: Who are eBay's main competitors?
output.answer: In its most recent annual report (the 10-K for fiscal 2025, filed in early 2026), eBay names its main competitors as large general online marketplaces such as Amazon and Alibaba, peer-to-peer and social platforms such as Facebook Marketplace, Instagram and TikTok, price-comparison sites such as Google Shopping, and sales tools such as Shopify that let sellers sell through other channels. It also says that some competitors with more resources than eBay include Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Apple and Meta. In general terms, eBay says it faces 'vigorous competition' from retailers, distributors, liquidators, import/export companies, auctioneers, catalog and mail-order companies, search engines and shopping channels. It competes on price, product selection, services, technology and geographic reach. Third-party analyses also often list Walmart, Temu and Shein as rivals, but those names did not appear in the parts of the 10-K I read.

key_facts.fact: eBay's Competition section in the 10-K doesn't name companies. It says eBay faces 'vigorous competition… from numerous sources,' including retailers, distributors, liquidators, import/export companies, auctioneers, catalog/mail-order companies, search engines and shopping channels.
The 10-K risk factors say some of eBay's competitors, such as Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Apple and Meta (Facebook and Instagram), have more resources than eBay.

The risk factors list other options buyers can turn to: general ecommerce marketplaces (Amazon, Alibaba), peer-to-peer platforms (Facebook Marketplace), shopping-comparison sites (Google Shopping) and social networks that allow purchases (Instagram, TikTok).
The 10-K says sellers may choose other channels, such as multi-channel services like Shopify.

passages.quote: We encounter vigorous competition in our business from numerous sources.
Some of our competitors, such as Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Apple and Meta (Facebook and Instagram),
including general ecommerce marketplaces, such as Amazon and Alibaba,
These consumers can also turn to shopping-comparison sites, such as Google Shopping,
social networks that enable purchases, such as Instagram and TikTok.
Sellers may also choose to sell their goods through alternative channels, such as multi-channel services like Shopify

caveats: I read about the first 200,000 of the filing's roughly 286,000 characters. Walmart, Temu, Shein, Etsy, Mercari, StockX and Whatnot did not appear in that part, but I can't confirm they are absent from the rest.
Third-party sites (e.g., growthsharematrix.com, stratrix.com) list Walmart, Temu and Shein as competitors. These are secondary analyses, not eBay's own disclosures.
The exact filing date wasn't in the text I read. Share counts are given as of February 13, 2026, so the filing is from about mid-to-late February 2026.
eBay may have named different competitors in quarterly filings or earnings calls after the 10-K. I did not check those.
